odoo.title: What is Odoo?
odoo.subtitle: Odoo is a program that brings together everything you currently manage separately: sales, inventory, invoices, customers and accounting. Think of it as your business's "brain": what happens in one area updates the others automatically.
odoo.example.title: A simple example
odoo.example.text: You sell 3 items at the counter. At that same moment, Odoo deducts them from inventory, creates the invoice, saves the customer's details and adds the sale to your daily report. Nothing gets entered twice.
odoo.before.title: Without a system
odoo.before.items: Inventory in a notebook or a spreadsheet nobody updates|You don't know what you sold until you do the math|Invoices made by hand, one by one|Orders and customer details lost between WhatsApp and sticky notes|Everything depends on you being there
odoo.after.title: With Odoo
odoo.after.items: You know what's in stock, even from your phone|You see today's sales in real time|Invoices in a couple of clicks|All your customer information in one place|Your business keeps running even when you're away
odoo.implement.title: So what does "implementing" Odoo mean?
odoo.implement.text: It means adapting it to the way your business works. I set it up, move your information over (products, customers, prices), train you and your team, and stay around to answer questions. You don't need to know anything about technology.

story.title: About me
story.intro: I'm a software engineer. Since 2020 I've helped organizations leave paper and spreadsheets behind and work with systems that save them time and money.
story.2020.desc: My starting point. I built web platforms to manage information for thousands of students. This is where I learned that the most valuable technology is the kind that solves real problems.
story.2021.desc: I built a business management system (ERP) for companies. I learned to understand how businesses operate day to day, turning their processes into easy-to-use digital tools.
story.2023.desc: I led the digital transformation of a group of companies: we went from paper-based processes to running 100% on Odoo, with connected online stores and AI assistants.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.subtitle: The questions I get most before we start.
faq.q1: Do I need to know about computers or technology?
faq.a1: No. I take care of all the technical side. If you can use WhatsApp, you can use Odoo, and I'll train you with examples from your own business.
faq.q2: Isn't my business too small for this?
faq.a2: No. Odoo works even for a one-person business. We start with the basics, like sales and inventory, and add more when you need it.
faq.a3: It depends on what your business needs. There are two parts: Odoo itself (it has a free version and paid plans based on the number of users) and my implementation service. In our first conversation I'll give you a clear, no-obligation proposal.
faq.a4: A small business can be up and running on Odoo in a few weeks. Larger projects are done in stages so your operations never stop.
faq.q5: What about the information I already have in spreadsheets or another system?
faq.a5: I move it into Odoo for you: products, customers, suppliers and prices. You don't start from scratch.
faq.a6: Yes. Odoo can generate and stamp electronic invoices valid with Mexico's tax authority (SAT). I leave it set up and ready to use.
faq.q7: What if I need help later on?
faq.a7: I stay with you after launch to answer questions, make adjustments and add new features as your business grows.
